sequence: M2DGR room_02, first 60 s of the raw bag

evaluation_protocol.alignment: rigid SE(3) fitted on the leading 20% of matched poses, never on the evaluation window

findings: Four-arm matrix on hall_01 [120,140] s: clean 0.3143 m ATE / 0.4341 m window; LiDAR-only occlusion 0.3653 / 0.5868; camera-only degradation 0.3148 / 0.4399; both 0.3661 / 0.6752.

The camera-only arm is indistinguishable from clean (ATE +0.2%), so the visual term is not carrying the solution on this sequence. Degrading both modalities gives essentially the LiDAR-only ATE (0.3661 vs 0.3653) with a worse window (0.6752 vs 0.5868, +15%).

Together with room_02 (0.0771 -> 0.0886 m) and the img_en=0 control (0.0761 vs 0.0771 m), this does not reproduce the cross-modal contamination mechanism Action Item 8.1 hypothesised: a tightly-coupled LIVO here behaves as a LiDAR-inertial system that tolerates single-modality near-field occlusion, and its visual term contributes ~nothing in either the clean or the degraded case.

The framework's case for this host therefore has to be made where the LiDAR-inertial solution itself fails (long geometric degeneracy, IMU saturation) or where an authoritative map must be protected, not where a polluted voxel map is expected to drag the photometric term down.

Playback rate is part of the protocol: hall_01 must run at 0.5x. At 1.0x the node consumed only 35.6 s of the 60 s window and the truncated trajectory produced an ATE that rose 0.09 -> 0.56 with time, which would have been reported as drift.
M2DGR Mocap GT contains isolated corrupted samples (room_02 t=26.35 s moves 7.11 m for one sample); the evaluator rejects them and reports the count. hall_01 needed none.

At 0.5x the run covers 57.7 s of 60 s and is the number reported here.
